title: Rationale
html:
Rationale

The shock to S&P 500 from “The Fed's rate is 5.00% or higher after April: a rise at every meeting, or a half-point step”

Two or more rises beyond the two-rise baseline means the Fed moved at every meeting or by a half point: inflation still accelerating into spring. One extra rise being priced between Jackson Hole and the September rise took the S&P down 1.2% (window). A second and third, with the 30-year mortgage already at 7.35% and equities at high multiples, does more than twice that; I put the S&P 5% below the baseline.
